sample_unit: model responses to ophthalmology patient queries

links.outcome: Rate of hallucinations or clinically misleading content in medical LLM ophthalmic answers
links.effect: MedLLaMA3-v20 had 25.5 percent of responses containing hallucinations or clinically misleading content, including fabricated terminology; gaps remained in clinical depth and consensus.
links.quote: MedLLaMA3-v20 performed poorest, with 25.5 percent of responses containing hallucinations or clinically misleading content, including fabricated terminology.

links.outcome: Agreement between GPT-4-Turbo grading and ophthalmologist grading of LLM responses
links.effect: GPT-4-Turbo grading aligned strongly with clinicians (Spearman rho 0.80, Kendall tau 0.67); Senior Consultants graded more conservatively, supporting hybrid automated and clinician review.
links.quote: GPT-4-Turbo grading showed strong alignment with clinician assessments overall, with Spearman rho of 0.80 and Kendall tau of 0.67, though Senior Consultants graded more conservatively.

unlisted_practices: LLM-as-judge automated evaluation of chatbot responses compared against clinician grading
Selecting small (<10B parameter) medical LLMs for resource-efficient deployment

screen.reason: The study evaluates the performance and safety (hallucinations/accuracy) of four small medical LLMs on ophthalmic queries alongside LLM-as-a-judge evaluation, but does not test a specific organizational deployment practice or guardrail.
